newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY-LEONARD TO CAPTAIN LIONS IN FIRST MATCH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-LEONARD TO CAPTAIN LIONS IN FIRST MATCH.

text.p: England tighthead prop Jason Leonard was named on Wednesday as captain of the British Lions for the first match of their eight-week tour of South Africa.

The Lions selectors decided to rest tour captain Martin Johnson for the game on Saturday against an Eastern Province invitation side after the Leicester player's demanding season in the northern hemisphere.

"Martin, like many of the players, has come off the back of a very long season, and our strategy is based on a long-range assessment of the formidable fixture programme which lies ahead," Lions manager Fran Cotton said on Wednesday.
"But we've told the squad we'll endeavour to make sure that all the players play in the first two games - whether in the starting line-up or as a substitute."
Leonard, who captained England in last December's match against Argentina and has earned 55 caps, was surprised to be leading the Lions in their tour opener.
"I didn't expect to captain the Lions at all on tour but it's a massive honour for all of the players involved to set the tour off on the right note," Leonard said.
"It's a very big challenge. Everybody is a little nervous but keen to get the tour under way."

The Lions' initial opponents in Port Elizabeth this Saturday will include Springboks Kobus Wiese and Hennie le Roux, former Wallaby flank Sam Scott-Young and New Zealand Barbarians captain and flank Matthew Webber.

British Lions: Neil Jenkins; John Bentley, Jeremy Guscott, Scott Gibbs, Nick Beal; Gregor Townsend, Rob Howley; Tim Rodber, Richard Hill, Lawrence Dallaglio, Doddy Weir, Simon Shaw, Jason Leonard (captain), Keith Wood, Tom Smith.
